CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

What this is

motrack is an R package (v0.3.0) for generating and visualizing trajectories for Multiple Object Tracking (MOT) experiments. It produces object positions and trajectories as tibbles and exports them as delimited text. No compiled code.

Commands

Run from the repo root. R is at /usr/local/bin/R; devtools, testthat, roxygen2, circular and ggforce are installed locally.

# Install dependencies
Rscript -e 'devtools::install_deps(dependencies = TRUE)'

# Load package for interactive work (no install needed)
Rscript -e 'devtools::load_all()'

# Run all tests (currently: 75 pass, 0 fail, 5 warnings from tidyselect's .data usage)
Rscript -e 'devtools::test()'

# Run one test file (filter matches the name after "test-")
Rscript -e 'devtools::test(filter = "bounce-pair")'

# Run a single test_that() block: no CLI flag; load_all() first, then
# testthat::test_file() on the file, or temporarily comment out others

# Regenerate NAMESPACE and man/ from roxygen comments (RoxygenNote 7.1.1)
Rscript -e 'devtools::document()'

# Full R CMD check (what CI runs on macOS, Windows, Ubuntu)
Rscript -e 'devtools::check()'

# Build the pkgdown site (CI: .github/workflows/pkgdown.yaml)
Rscript -e 'pkgdown::build_site()'

Edit roxygen comments in R/*.R, then run devtools::document(). Do not hand-edit NAMESPACE or man/*.Rd.

Architecture

The package is a single simulation pipeline. Understanding it requires reading R/trajectory.R and R/position.R together.

Data model. Everything is a tibble with an object column (object IDs): - Position: object, x, y plus optional direction (radians; 0 = 3 o’clock, counter-clockwise) and speed. Validated by is_valid_position(). - Trajectory: time, object, x, y plus direction, speed, and step-specific state columns (ttt for zigzag; ttc, mov_state, speed_scale for wait-and-move). Validated by is_valid_trajectory(). - position8c and trajectory8c (in data/) are example datasets.

Settings. Settings are a plain named list. default_settings() (R/position.R) defines the valid keys; new_settings() overrides them and rejects unknown names. It also accepts two optional keys, speed and arena_inside_radius, which are not in the defaults. speed can be a number or a list of functions function(time, moment); cur_speed() evaluates them.

Generation pipeline. 1. generate_positions_random(n, settings) places objects in a square/circle/donut arena (xlim/ylim, arena_shape), optionally enforcing min_distance. 2. make_random_trajectory(start, timescale, settings, step_function, ...) iterates over timescale. Each step first applies the enabled bounce functions (bounce_off_square, bounce_off_circle, bounce_off_inside, bounce_off_others) to the current moment, then calls step_function(moment, time_next, settings, ...). The result is a list-column of per-time moments that is unnested at the end. 3. Step functions (step_direct, step_zigzag, step_waitandmove, step_vonmises) return the next moment. They carry per-object state in extra columns, initialized on the first call (the if (!"ttt" %in% names(moment)) pattern). Custom steps should follow the same signature and use extrapolate_moment() to move objects and cur_speed() for speed.

Bouncing (bounce_pair, bounce_off_* in R/trajectory.R) works on direction vectors and the next-step positions. bounce_off_others uses single-linkage clustering (hclust/cutree) on next-step distances to find collisions.

Post-processing and output. - simplify_trajectory() reduces the per-frame data to critical points. It can keep only snapshots, which is useful for export. - estimate_position_for_time() interpolates positions at arbitrary times. - plot_position(), plot_trajectory(), annotate_image(), annotate_aperture() draw with ggplot2 and grid/png. - render_trajectory_video() uses the animation package and needs an external ffmpeg (path set via animation::ani.options). - save_trajectory() / load_trajectory() read and write delimited text (delim argument). - validate_trajectory() and validate_object_direction_change() check output.

Tidy evaluation. Code uses dplyr verbs with .data$col pronouns. R/utils-tidy-eval.R re-exports rlang symbols; R/utils-pipe.R re-exports %>%. Follow these patterns rather than adding new imports.

Work in progress: R/discrete.R. This file (grid positions, step_vortex, step_grid) is not exported (see NAMESPACE) and is not yet documented. It uses |> and unqualified dplyr verbs (left_join, join_by, mutate) that are not imported, and the recent commit notes the vortex step does not yet respect arena limits. Treat it as experimental. Check it before relying on it.

Tests

Tests live in tests/testthat/ and cover settings validation, bounce calculations, position generation, trajectory generation, and saving. Randomized tests call set.seed() (e.g., test-generate-positions.R, test-generate-trajectories.R). There is no lint configuration.
